1#main: The law of close and distant tidings. And it contains 12 seifim. One to whom tidings came that his relative died — if within thirty days tidings arrived, even day thirty itself — this is close tidings; obligated to observe seven mourning days from day tidings arrived; tears; counts thirty days (from day of tidings) (so Rambam and Nimmukei Yosef beginning Moed Katan and Mordechai) for haircut with other matters; rule: day of close tidings is like day of burial; if heard from day thirty onward — need observe only one hour, whether heard by day or night; if heard at night and observed part of mourning at night — one hour counts for him; and even for father and mother; and this for seven-day decree; but for thirty-day decree — for father and mother observe haircut until companions protest and pressing until festival comes and they protest; and greeting and entering banquet house; counts from day of death not day of tidings; therefore if tidings came for father and mother after twelve months — observes only one day even for thirty-day decree.
2#main: One who hears distant tidings need not observe all mourning laws — ink suffices by removing shoe; need not wrapping or overturning bed; permitted work, bathing, anointing, use of bed, Torah study; if no shoes on feet — must overturn bed or wrap head, for need act recognizable as mourning; if engaged in Torah or work or bathing and anointing and tidings came — pauses one hour for mourning and returns to his activity; but if wearing tefillin — need not remove them; nevertheless does not fulfill mourning by this pause; need recognizable mourning act such as removing shoe or overturning bed or wrapping — one suffices.
3#main: They do not give meal of recovery for distant tidings.
4#main: They do not tear for distant tidings; for father and mother tear always: {Rama: (and where cannot tear — forbidden to be strict and tear) (Avraham Zacuto).}
5#main: One who hears tidings on Shabbat or festival — and on Motza'ei Shabbat and festival becomes distant — observes only one day; on Shabbat and festival forbidden private matters.
6#main: One who hears distant tidings on Shabbat or festival — does not observe even private matters; on Motza'ei Shabbat and festival observes one hour and suffices.
7#main: One who hears close tidings on Shabbat — Shabbat counts as one day; next day he tears; and it becomes sixth day of mourning.
8#main: Ten days after Sukkot heard one died erev festival — even if counting one hour before festival as seven and seven festival days and Shemini Atzeret as twenty-one and ten more days would be forty-one — this is not distant tidings law but close tidings, for festival does not count for one who did not observe mourning before at all; and all the more one who did not know relative died (Rabbeinu Yerucham in name of Baal HaMaor and so Ramban).
9#main: Heard two distant tidings one day — observes only one day; if they were close or two died as one — counts both as one seven and thirty; heard one today and one tomorrow — counts two from day of each tidings seven and thirty.
10#main: Heard close tidings Shabbat erev festival — since private matters apply on Shabbat, that Shabbat counts toward seven.
11#main: One who already prayed evening and still daytime and heard close tidings — counts from tomorrow; that day does not count.
12#main: One whose relative died and he did not know — not obligated they tell him, even father and mother; on this it says one who brings forth slander is a fool; permitted to invite him to betrothal and wedding meals and all joy since he does not know; however if asked — may not lie and say alive, as it says keep far from false matter: {Rama: Nevertheless for sons custom to inform so they say Kaddish; for daughters no custom to inform (Mahariw siman 13); mitzvah fast day father or mother died (Kol Bo in name of Rambam); fast day of death not day of burial (Mahariw siman 121 and Maharai siman 296 and later authorities); unless one was at burial not death (kabbalah from elder Maharam Landa); if that day is day tachanun not said — do not fast at all; if died in Adar and year intercalated — primary to fast in first Adar (Terumat HaDeshen siman 294 and R' Yehudah Mintz) though some dispute, so is primary; if died leap year in second Adar — fast also second Adar in leap year (same there); see Orach Chaim siman 568 seif 7; see above siman 391 not eat meal night father mother died; if fast falls erev Shabbat its law like other fasts see Orach Chaim siman 249; if first time completed — practice all his days.}
